adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, after a successful enable (`handleEnable`), the UI transitions to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` (`setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes);`) and only calls `onEnable()` from the explicit “close” button in that step. That can leave the parent (e.g., the switch state) stale even though the server-side enable already succeeded, matching the reported stale UI / retry error scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:137 — Once all codes are used the stored array is all nulls, so the user gets IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes and has no clear recovery signal.

On successful backup-code login, the matched entry is set to `null` and the array is re-encrypted (`backupCodes[index] = null; ... symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes))`). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent logins can reuse the same code or overwrite each other and restore an already-consumed code

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup code flow does a read-modify-write: it decrypts `user.backupCodes`, finds the matching code, mutates the in-memory array (`backupCodes[index] = null`), then writes the entire re-encrypted array back via `prisma.user.update(...)`. There is no transaction/compare-and-swap/conditional update to ensure the stored value hasn’t changed since it was read. Two concurrent authorizations can both validate against the same original decrypted list and then overwrite each other’s updates; e.g., one consumes code A and writes `[null, B]` while another consumes code B based on the original `[A, B]` and writes `[A, null]`, effectively restoring A. Similarly, two concurrent logins can both accept the same backup code before either update commits.
